<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par119 />{{GHGheb|text=קָרָא בְ}} to call ''on'' some one, {{GHGheb|text=נִשְׁבַּע בְּ|translate=iurare per aliquem|en=to swear by}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁאַל בְּ|translate=to enquire of}} some one. Again; {{GHGheb|text=רָאָה בְ|translate=to look upon}}, {{GHGheb|text=שָׁמַע בְּ|translate=to hearken to}} (but cf. also {{GHGpar|404|m|nonumber=1}}), generally with the secondary idea of participation, or of the pleasure with which one sees or hears anything, especially pleasure at the misfortunes of others, hence {{GHGheb|text=רָאָה בְ|translate=to see his desire on any one ''or'' anything}}; cf. however, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=16}} ''let me not look upon the death of the child''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=19}} {{GHGtranslate|because they had looked ''[irreverently]'' at the ark of the Lord}}.

Closely related to this is the use of {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}:

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|l}}
(3) To introduce the person or thing, which is the object of a ''mental'' act, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽאֱמִין בְּ|translate=to trust in}} (to cleave trustingly ''to'') somebody or something; {{GHGheb|text=בָּטַח בְּ|translate=to have confidence in}}...; {{GHGheb|text=שָׂמַח בְּ|translate=to rejoice in}} or ''at'' something, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=דִּבֶּר בְּ|translate=to speak of (about)}} some one or something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=6|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=3 f.}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|m}}
(4) The idea of an action as extending ''to'' something, with at the same time the secondary idea of participation ''in'' something, underlies finally the {{GHGterm|partitive}} use of {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אָכַל בְּ|translate=to share in eating}} something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=43 ff.}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=22|verse=11}}; also simply {{GHGtranslate|to eat, to taste of}} something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=25}}; so also {{GHGheb|text=לָחַם בְּ|translate=to eat of}}, and {{GHGheb|text=שָׁתָה בְ}}<ref>To be distinguished from {{GHGheb|text=שָׁתָה בְ}}={{GHGtranslate|to drink from}} (a cup, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=6|verse=6}}), as in Arabic and Aramaic ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=5|verse=2}}). Cf. also {{polytonic|ἐν ποτηρίοις}} (Xen. Anab. vi. 1, 4), {{polytonic|ἐν χρυσώμασι πίνειν}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=3 Ezr|chapter=3|verse=6}}), ''venenum in auro bibitur'', Seneca, Thyestes 453, and the French ''boire dans une tasse''.</ref> ''to drink of'' something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=9|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁמַע בְּ|translate=to hear}} a whisper ''of something'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=26|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=מָצָא בְּ|translate=they found}} remaining ''of her'' only..., {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=9|verse=35}}; {{GHGheb|text=נָשָׂא בְ|translate=to bear a share of}} something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=18|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=13}}. Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=חָלַק בְּ|translate=to give a share of}} something, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=39|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=בָּנָח בְ|translate=to do building to}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=4|verse=4}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|n}}
(5) With the idea of ''touching, striking against anything'' is naturally connected that of proximity and vicinity ''near'', and further that of association ''with'' something; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=9|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּנַפְשׁוֹ|translate=with the life thereof}}; 15:14, 32:11 {{GHGheb|text=בְּמַקְלִי|translate=with my staff}}. Sometimes {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} combined with a verb of motion (''to come with'' something), expresses the idea of ''bringing'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=15|verse=1}} ''Samson visited his wife with a kid'', i.e. he brought her a kid; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=23|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=66|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=15|verse=19}} ff., 16:6.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|o}}
(6) From the idea of connexion with something, being accompanied by something (see n), is developed, finally, the ''instrumental'' use of {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}, which represents the means or instrument (or even the personal agent), as something ''with which'' one has associated himself in order to perform an action; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=4|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=בַּשֵּׁ֫בֶט|translate=they smite with the rod}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=24}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=30}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּךָ|translate=by thee}} (so also 44:6, parallel with {{GHGheb|text=בְּשִׁמְךָ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=1|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=12|verse=14|hidebook=1}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=עָבַד בְּ|translate=to labour by means of}} some one, i.e. to cause him to labour at it, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=14}}, &c. On {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} with the passive to introduce the means or the author, see {{GHGpar|121|f}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|p}}
A variety of the {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} {{GHGterm|instrumenti}} is {{GHGheb|text=ב}} {{GHGterm|pretii}} (the price being considered as the ''means'' of acquiring a thing), cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=18|hidebook=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=בְּרָחֵל}}); 30:16, 33:19, 34:15 ({{GHGheb|text=בְּזֹאת|translate=on this}} condition); 37:28; also, in a wider sense, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=28}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּ|translate=for the sake of}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=13}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|q}}
Rem. The use of {{GHGheb|text=בְּ|translate=instrumenti}} to introduce the object is peculiar in such expressions as {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=44|verse=20}} ''and thou coveredst over us'' {{GHGheb|text=בְּצַלְמָ֫וֶת|translate=with the shadow of death}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=פָּֽעֲרוּ עָלַי בְּפִיהֶם|translate=they have opened wide their mouth against me}} (prop. ''have made an opening with their mouth''); cp. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=7|verse=20}} ''he lifted up'' {{GHGheb|text=בַּמַּטֶּה|translate=the rod}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=16|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=חָגַר}} and {{GHGheb|text=צָנַף}} followed by {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=8|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=17}}. Analogous to some English expressions we find both ''to gnash the teeth'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=16}}, and ''to gnash with the teeth'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=9}}; ''to wink the eye'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=10|verse=10}}, and ''to wink with the eye'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=6|verse=13}}; ''shake the head'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=8}}, and ''to shake with the head'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=18|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=4}}.—In all these instances<section end=par119 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
